title: Checkpoint: The Widest Window
prompt:
**Task.** Stand on cell 1 of a strip of n cells; cell i has value
g_i (may be negative). Repeatedly jump forward at most k cells (from i to
i+1..i+k); each landing cell adds its value. Maximize the total collected
when you reach cell n (you must end exactly there). Print the maximum.

**Constraints:** 2 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ k ≤ min(2000, n−1); −50000 ≤ g_i ≤
50000. Totals reach ~10^10 — 64-bit.

**Budget check:** the dp[i] = g_i + max(dp[i−k..i−1]) recurrence is
O(n·k) = 4·10^8 naive — risky; the fused window-min is O(n).

tests.name: small walk
k covers all
tests.hint: k = 3 lets path 1→2→3→4 land on every cell: 1+2+3+4 = 10. (The full-distance 1→4 jump is exactly what the off-by-one window loses.)

tests.name: starved window
tests.hint: Path 1→3 (a distance-2 jump, k = 1 means... no: k = 1 allows only distance 1; path 1→2→3 = 2−1+2 = 3. With k = 1 the off-by-one window can reach nothing at i = 2 → garbage.

tests.name: full scale
tests.hint: n = 200000, k = 2000: naive O(n·k) re-max is 4·10^8 — the fused monotonic-deque sweep is O(n). Ground truth computed in Python with the same recurrence.
